questions.text: Walk me through your last full sales cycle, from first touch to close. Where did it almost fall apart?
questions.rationale: A full-cycle narrative exposes process discipline; the near-loss moment exposes honesty.

questions.text: Tell me about a deal you lost that you should have won. What did you learn?
questions.rationale: Loss analysis separates reflective sellers from excuse-makers.

questions.text: How do you qualify out of a deal? Tell me about a time you walked away.
questions.rationale: Walking away is the rarest qualification skill; a real story evidences pipeline discipline.

questions.text: Describe your approach to prospecting. What does your first outreach to a cold account actually look like?
questions.rationale: The concrete artifact question separates practitioners from theorists.

questions.text: Tell me about the most skeptical buyer you converted. What moved them?
questions.rationale: Reveals whether the candidate sells through discovery and proof or through pressure.

questions.text: How do you run a discovery call? What questions do you always ask?
questions.rationale: Discovery quality predicts close rates; canned pitch instincts show up immediately.

questions.text: Describe a time you had to deliver a price increase to an existing customer. How did it go?
questions.rationale: Tests value articulation under adversarial conditions.

questions.text: What attracted you to sales, and what keeps you in it on the bad weeks?
questions.rationale: Resilience sources matter in a rejection-heavy role.

questions.text: Tell me about a quarter you missed quota. What was your read on why, and what did you change?
questions.rationale: Everyone misses eventually; the diagnostic quality of the answer is the signal.

questions.text: How do you use your CRM? What do you log religiously and what do you skip?
questions.rationale: Operational hygiene question; the skip half invites honesty worth probing.

questions.text: Describe a time you disagreed with your sales manager about deal strategy. What happened?
questions.rationale: Screens for coachability paired with conviction.

questions.text: Tell me about a deal where the champion left the company mid-cycle. What did you do?
questions.rationale: Multi-threading discipline shows up exactly here; single-threaded sellers stall.

questions.text: How do you handle a prospect who has clearly been burned by a product like ours before?
questions.rationale: Objection handling grounded in empathy rather than script.

questions.text: What is your process between signature and handoff to customer success? Walk me through your last handoff.
questions.rationale: Post-signature behavior separates sellers who care about retention from those who care about commission timing.

questions.text: Tell me about the best sales team culture you have worked in. What specifically made it good?
questions.rationale: Reveals whether the candidate thrives in collaborative or purely competitive floors.

questions.text: Describe a time you helped a teammate close their deal with no benefit to your own number.
questions.rationale: Direct probe for team-first behavior in a role that incentivizes the opposite.

questions.text: How do you learn a new product well enough to sell it credibly? How long does that take you?
questions.rationale: Ramp speed and learning method predict time to productivity.

questions.text: Tell me about a negotiation where procurement stripped everything back to price. How did you respond?
questions.rationale: Value defense under commoditization pressure is a senior seller's defining skill.

questions.text: What role does social proof play in your selling? Give an example of using a reference well.
questions.rationale: Reference orchestration is a concrete, checkable skill.

questions.text: Describe your ideal relationship with marketing. Where has that relationship broken down for you before?
questions.rationale: Sales-marketing friction is universal; the candidate's framing reveals collaboration instincts.

questions.text: What motivates you more: the win, the money, or the customer outcome? Be honest.
questions.rationale: There is no wrong answer, but self-awareness here predicts management fit.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you oversold and the customer churned. What is your guardrail against that now?
questions.rationale: Tests honesty about the role's central ethical temptation.

questions.text: How do you build a territory or book from scratch? Walk me through your first 30 days.
questions.rationale: A concrete territory plan separates builders from inheritors.

questions.text: As a sales lead, how do you coach a rep who is behind plan without crushing them? Give a real example.
questions.rationale: Coaching stories under performance pressure define sales leadership quality.

questions.text: How do you forecast? What is your method for calling a deal committed versus best case?
questions.rationale: Forecast discipline is the leadership skill executives actually depend on.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you spotted a pattern across lost deals and changed something systemic.
questions.rationale: Pattern-level thinking separates leads from individual contributors with big numbers.

questions.text: What does a great first sales hire look like for a company our size? Would you hire yourself for it?
questions.rationale: Tests market awareness and honest self-assessment simultaneously.

questions.text: Describe your relationship with rejection. What is your actual recovery routine after a brutal no?
questions.rationale: Concrete recovery routines predict durability better than bravado.

questions.text: Walk me through how you would sell our product to a buyer who currently uses nothing and feels no pain.
questions.rationale: Status-quo displacement is the hardest sale; tests demand creation ability.

questions.text: Tell me about a piece of deal feedback from a manager that changed how you sell.
questions.rationale: Coachability, evidenced by a specific applied change.
